clue.text: Let's dance in pants in private

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters before it are made into a mess and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to dance with your trousers on, or the Bowie song Let's Dance, done somewhere nobody is watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers but is British slang for rubbish, signalling an anagram of LETSDANCE plus IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done secretly, hidden from public view, is done in private.

clue.text: China Girl's dictionary

parts.note: CH is a standard abbreviation for China
the 's of Girl's supplies the final letter

explanation.surface: Seems to ask which dictionary contains Bowie's song China Girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is used as a letter: CH, AMBER, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers is the standard British reference dictionary much loved by crossword setters.

clue.text: Ziggy Stardust possibly short-changed over advance

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the second
short means the word for changed loses its final letter here

parts.note: to advance is to go forward

explanation.surface: Ziggy Stardust shortchanged as a deposit was paid in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-changed' reads as cheated, but it splits into two jobs: 'short' trims the word for changed, which then sits over the advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ziggy Stardust was a stage persona Bowie adopted, a second self, which the definition offers as an example.

clue.text: Dutch star transformed game

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of star are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A Dutch celebrity is turned into a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Only star is rearranged; the Dutch abbreviation stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game of throwing small missiles at a board.

clue.text: Susan Stranks on vacation admitting small amount of fame

indicators.note: admitting means the first pieces let the small amount in between them

parts.note: Sue is the short form of Susan
CC, cubic centimetres, a small volume

indicators.note: on vacation means the word Stranks is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Stranks

explanation.surface: TV presenter Susan Stranks, away on holiday, letting slip a little celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: SUE plus SS (Stranks emptied) take in CC, giving SU-CC-E-SS. Susan Stranks was a British children's TV presenter of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame and success both describe achieving renown or a prosperous outcome; here they are loose synonyms.

clue.text: Diamond Dogs' leader has dinner and drink

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Dogs' is taken

parts.note: tea is the evening meal in much of Britain

explanation.surface: The lead dog of Bowie's Diamond Dogs eats and then has something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In northern British usage tea is the evening meal, so dinner gives TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea is a chilled beverage, so it is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Changes cautioned in teaching

indicators.note: Changes, Bowie's song title, works as a verb saying the letters of cautioned are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bowie's Changes warned listeners during a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Education is the process of instructing pupils, the same as schooling or tuition.

clue.text: Cat People starts without a beat

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the starting letters go around a
starts means the opening letter of each of Cat and People is taken

explanation.surface: The film Cat People begins without a musical rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking: C and P wrap round A.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap something is to outdo or top it, as in capping someone's story.

clue.text: Kooks occasionally covered by female singer's band

indicators.note: covered by means the singer's name goes around the letters
occasionally means every other letter of Kooks is taken

parts.note: second and fourth letters of Kooks

explanation.surface: Bowie's song Kooks gets the odd cover version from a female singer's group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a musical group, but it is a strip worn round the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A choker is a close-fitting necklace, a decorative strip worn tight round the throat.

clue.text: Wine Society under pressure to make aperitif

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the wine and society come below the P

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A wine club is pressed into producing a pre-dinner drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastis is an aniseed-flavoured French spirit typically drunk before a meal to sharpen appetite.

clue.text: Player from Barça oddly missing height

indicators.note: oddly missing means the odd-numbered letters of Barça are dropped, keeping the even ones

parts.note: second and fourth letters of Barça
a tor is a rocky hill, a height

explanation.surface: A footballer from Barcelona, strangely absent from the high point.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of BARCA leaves AC; a tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a player in the theatrical sense, one who plays parts on stage.

clue.text: Cloud user's terribly naive

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of Cloud user are badly jumbled

parts.note: the word user, with its 's serving as is

explanation.surface: Someone who trusts their files to cloud storage is dreadfully gullible.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being credulous means believing things too readily, which is the same as being gullible or innocent.

clue.text: Spooner's geek is top in place of breeding

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as Dr Spooner did

parts.note: a geek is a nerd, and is gives the 's

explanation.surface: Spooner declares that a geek is supreme in some breeding ground.
explanation.walkthrough: NERD'S BEST with the opening sounds swapped is said as BIRD'S NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's nest is where birds lay eggs and raise chicks, a breeding site.

clue.text: Amnesty welcoming sanctuary for Arab

indicators.note: welcoming means the charity's initials take the sanctuary inside

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A human-rights group giving refuge to someone from the Arab world.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adeni is a person from Aden in Yemen, so is an Arab.

clue.text: Young Americans' golf hero retiring after game

indicators.note: after means the game comes first, with the rest following

parts.note: G is golf in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for hero is read backwards

explanation.surface: Bowie's Young Americans: a golfing hero quits once the round is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Young Americans is a Bowie album title, here meaning US children; RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugrats is American slang for small children, and the name of a US cartoon about toddlers.

clue.text: Dad upset over injured goolies getting words of sorrow

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the second
upset in a down clue means turned upwards, so the word for Dad is read backwards
injured means the letters of goolies are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A father in a state after a painful blow below the belt says he is sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: Goolies is British slang for testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Apologies are expressions of regret, statements saying one is sorry.

clue.text: Song about racism in Absolute Beginners

indicators.note: Beginners means the starting letters of about, racism, in and Absolute are taken

explanation.surface: A song in Bowie's film Absolute Beginners deals with racism.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo vocal piece in an opera, so a kind of song.

clue.text: Cabbage in pub served up with batter coating

indicators.note: coating means the batter's name goes around the reversed pub

parts.note: Virat Kohli is a famous Indian cricket batter

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means turned upwards, so the word for pub is read backwards

explanation.surface: Cabbage dished up in a pub, covered in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' looks like a frying coat but is a cricketer: Virat Kohli, Indian batting star.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a vegetable of the brassica family, a variety of cabbage with a swollen stem.

clue.text: Flying safety limiting Father Christmas perhaps

indicators.note: limiting means the rearranged letters enclose the word for Father
flying means the letters of safety are sent into a new order

explanation.surface: Air safety rules restricting Father Christmas in his sleigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father Christmas' reads as Santa, but splits: Father gives DA and Christmas is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is an example of a religious festival day in the Church calendar.

clue.text: Downsides of taking the lid off Heroes

indicators.note: taking the lid off means the word for heroes loses its first letter, its top

explanation.surface: The drawbacks of opening a tub of Heroes chocolates, or of Bowie's song.
explanation.walkthrough: Heroes is also a Cadbury chocolate assortment sold in lidded tubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cons are disadvantages, as in pros and cons.

clue.text: Stop standing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a place where a train halts
second meaning: social rank or position

explanation.definitionFit: A station is both a railway halt and one's rank in society, as in getting above one's station.

clue.text: Perhaps Aladdin Sane's second half provides range of colourful numbers

parts.note: Aladdin is an example of a pantomime, a British Christmas stage show

indicators.note: second half means the last two of the four letters of sane are kept

explanation.surface: The second half of Bowie's Aladdin Sane gives a colourful set of tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a British family Christmas show; Aladdin is a classic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantone is a commercial colour-matching system in which each shade is identified by a number.

clue.text: Upstart beauty not finished after knock-back

indicators.note: after means the beauty follows the knock
back means the word for knock is read the other way
not finished means the word for beauty loses its last letter

parts.note: Venus, goddess of love, is a beauty

explanation.surface: An upstart beauty not having finished after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock-back' reads as a rejection, but splits into RAP reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a newcomer to wealth or status, a social climber looked down on as an upstart.

clue.text: Went in pursuit of 400, accepting Ashes nearly lost

indicators.note: accepting means the numerals take the other letters inside
lost means those remaining letters are thrown into a new order
nearly means the last letter of Ashes is dropped

explanation.surface: Cricket: chasing a target of 400 with the Ashes almost gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket series; chasing is batting to beat a total.
explanation.definitionFit: To have chased someone is to have pursued them, followed in an attempt to catch.

clue.text: Suggested date under old tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the date comes below the rest

explanation.surface: Someone proposed a meeting beneath an ancient tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To have opined is to have offered an opinion, put forward a view.

clue.text: Animal power in Modern Love

indicators.note: in means power is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: An animal's strength shown in Bowie's song Modern Love.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippo is a large African mammal, the hippopotamus.

clue.text: Bastion of cool Paris fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters of cool Paris are given a new form

explanation.surface: Paris as a stronghold of cool style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like a noun about Paris style but is a verb meaning shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is a citadel on high ground, a fortress such as the one at Athens.

clue.text: Secretly chomp a Starman's food

indicators.note: Secretly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Quietly munching the meal belonging to Bowie's Starman.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian staple, a type of foodstuff made from wheat dough.

clue.text: Emotional and extraordinary visit welcoming life on Mars finishes Earth

indicators.note: welcoming means the rearranged visit takes the end letters inside
extraordinary means the letters of visit are put into an unusual order
finishes means the final letter of each of life, on and Mars

explanation.surface: A remarkable trip finding Life on Mars, Bowie's song, ends up on Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensitive person is easily moved, readily feeling or showing strong feelings.

clue.text: Part of Breaking Glass is building

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fragment of broken glass
second meaning: the ..., a skyscraper in London

explanation.walkthrough: Breaking Glass is a Bowie song; the Shard is a London skyscraper.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a sharp fragment of glass, and the Shard is London's tallest tower, by London Bridge.

clue.text: David evens out production of Sound and Vision

indicators.note: evens out means the even-numbered letters of David are removed, leaving the odd ones

explanation.surface: David Bowie smooths out the production of his song Sound and Vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A DVD is a disc format carrying recorded audio and video together.

clue.text: Sly guitar in remix of Space Oddity

indicators.note: a remix rearranges a recording, so the letters of Sly guitar in are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sneaky guitar part on a new remix of Bowie's Space Oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: A singularity is a point in space-time where gravity becomes infinite, such as at a black hole's centre: a cosmic oddity.
